newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds pick-up on firmer U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds pick-up on firmer U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose on Monday, marking a turnaround mid-session on the back of stronger U.S. Treasuries.
One trader said he was surprised at the strong reversal of the market's earlier decline considering the slim activity ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 117.80, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 82-3/4.
The "Pre 2" hit a low of 117 early on.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional due 2007 rose $0.60 to 101.45.
Traders said the market got the boost from U.S. Treasuries, but the growing consensus the market has discounted a 25-basis-point rise in U.S. rates helped attract buyers at the early low levels.
The trader estimated the market will likely open firm to higher on Tuesday on the conviction that a U.S. rate increase will not do much harm to Argentina's economy.

"A U.S. rate hike is pretty well discounted and I'd be surprised if Argentina has a major problem if the Fed moves rates tomorrow," analyst Geoffrey Dennis at Bear Stearns told Reuters Financial Television on Monday.

There was also uplifting news on the domestic front on Monday, in the form of preliminary industrial production figures showing a rise of 9.2 percent in August compared with the same month a year earlier, according to the FIEL economic research institute. In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 5.63 percent from 5.88 percent.
